overview: Italy is a very interesting destination for students interested in electricity, power systems, renewable energy, electrical machines, industrial automation and modern energy infrastructure. The engineering programs offered by Italian universities provide a mix of scientific fundamentals, technical knowledge and practical experience.

In Italy, Electrical Engineering in Italy at the bachelor's level is usually a three-year undergraduate degree (Laurea) worth 180 ECTS credits. Students are introduced to electrical circuits, electromagnetism, electrical machines, power generation, energy distribution, control systems and electrical safety.

For students in India who have completed Class 12, Bachelors programs in Electrical Engineering in Italy can provide a path to international engineering education. However, applicants should verify the teaching language, academic requirements, entrance examinations, tuition fees and application deadlines for each university.
Edu-Hawk Worldwide helps students to find the right universities, know eligibility, prepare their documents and strategize their applications to study in Italy.

sections.title: Why Study Electrical Engineering in Italy?

items: Electrical engineering is important in renewable energy, electric transportation, industrial automation, power distribution and energy efficient infrastructure. Italy's engineering universities have programs that introduce students to these technical areas and their industrial applications.
Why Study Electrical Engineering in Italy Bachelors programs?
Solid engineering foundations: Learn math, physics, electrical circuits and electromagnetism.
Energy and power systems: Find out about electrical machines, power grids, electricity distribution and energy management.
Renewable energy applications: Learn about the electrical systems used in solar, wind and other renewable energy technologies.
Industrial applications: Gain an understanding of electrical equipment, automation, control systems and industrial processes.
Practical learning: Depending on the university, students may participate in lab sessions, design exercises and technical projects.
Further studies: Graduates can pursue master's degrees in electrical engineering, energy systems, power engineering and related fields.

Students looking at Bachelors degrees in Electrical Engineering in Italy should think about course content, language of instruction, entrance test requirements, total study costs and postgraduate opportunities before deciding.

Popular specialization fields

Renewable Energy Engineering: Electrical integration of solar and wind energy, energy conversion and sustainable electricity systems.

Industrial Automation: Electrical engineering, control systems, sensors and automated industrial equipment.

Some specializations are offered only as electives or master's programs and not as separate bachelor's degrees.

items: Indian applicants need to meet the academic and admission requirements of the university of their choice.
Academic qualifications
Applicants typically need:
A recognized Higher Secondary School pass of Class 12 or equivalent.
A school qualification fulfilling the University's requirements for undergraduate study in Italy.
Mathematics and other prerequisite subjects as stated by the program.
Meeting any selection criteria Academic results
Additional qualification verification documents as requested.
The University assesses foreign qualifications according to its admission regulations and Italian requirements in force. There is no guaranty of admission even after passing Class 12.
Subject prerequisites

Electrical engineering students take classes in electromagnetism, circuit theory, power systems and engineering calculations. All of these require math. Physics is also important to understand electricity, energy, machines and electrical phenomena.
Applicants should check with the university to see if there are any subject requirements or minimum academic standards.
Language requirements
Language requirements vary depending on the program chosen:
Italian-taught programs: Applicants might need to demonstrate Italian proficiency.
English-taught programs: May require proof of English language proficiency.
Mixed-language programs Students should check the language used in each year and any additional language requirements.
Entrance tests

Some universities have an engineering entrance test or some other selection procedure. For example, Politecnico di Torino requires a mandatory admission test for its 2026/27 Electrical Engineering bachelor program.

The syllabus, registration dates, selection criteria, and examination pattern vary from one institution to another. Students interested in studying Electrical Engineering in Italy Bachelors should consult the official admissions information for the program they are interested in.

7. Admission to Electrical Engineering in Italy
These are the general steps that students can follow when applying to Italian universities.
Pick your branch of engineering: You can opt to specialize in power systems, renewable energy, electrical machines, automation or electric mobility.
Shortlist Universities. Look at course structure, teaching language, tuition fees and location.
Check eligibility: Ensure that your Class 12 qualification and subjects are in line with the university's requirements.
Prepare for the entrance test: Find out what examination is required, review the syllabus and register before the deadline.
Collect your documents: Academic records, passport, proof of language proficiency and any qualification verification documents that are required.
Submit the application: Finish the application and selection procedures of the university.
Get the admission decision: Follow the university instructions to accept and enroll.
Complete pre-enrolment, if necessary Students requiring an Italian study visa usually complete the pre-enrolment procedure through Universitaly.
Apply for a student visa: send the documents requested by the Italian diplomatic mission competent for your country. Admission doesn't mean you'll get a visa.
Prepare for arrival Make accommodation, insurance and travel arrangements before you leave.
Application deadlines and procedures vary by institution, applicant category and intake. Follow the latest official university and visa guidance.

faq.question: Can Indian students pursue Electrical Engineering in Italy after 12th?
faq.answer: Yeah. Indian students can apply provided they have Class 12 qualification meeting the university's entry requirements and also meet the relevant academic, language, entrance-test and document conditions.

faq.question: How long does a bachelors degree in electrical engineering last in Italy?
faq.answer: In Italy, most electrical engineering bachelor degrees are three years long and give 180 ECTS credits. Students should check the length and structure of the program they are applying for.

faq.question: Are there any electrical engineering bachelor's programs taught in English in Italy?
faq.answer: Many of the programs are taught in Italian. For instance, the aforementioned bachelor's programs of Politecnico di Milano and Politecnico di Torino are taught in Italian. It is recommended that applicants check the language of instruction before applying.

faq.question: How much does it cost to study electrical engineering in Italy?
faq.answer: The average cost of tuition at public universities can range from about €900 to €4,000 per year, whereas private institutions are generally more expensive. Actual fees depend on the institution, program and fee rules applicable.

faq.question: What to do after bachelor in electrical engineering in Italy?
faq.answer: Depending on your skills and experience, you may be looking for jobs in power systems, electrical design, equipment manufacturing, renewable energy, industrial automation, maintenance and electrical testing. Some graduates take a master's degree for further specialization.
